english.title: Fail to display notice in premises re sale of adult fireworks - Firework Reg's 2004
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), where adult fireworks were

(A)_[supplied]_
(B)_[exposed for supply]_

(C)_[failed to display in a prominent position a notice stating the information required by regulation 10(2) of the Firework Regulations 2004]_
(D)_[where a notice as required by regulation 10(2) of the Firework Regulations 2004 was not displayed, failed to give the required information to a person to whom fireworks were supplied or exposed for supply]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 10 of the Fireworks Regulations 2004 and section 11(2) and (4) of the Fireworks Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: See regulation 10(2) for details of the "required information".

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months (see regulation 13 of the Fireworks Regulations 2004)

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
